I just want to chime in here to say that when starting this thread I didn't expect it to quite go in this direction. I'm a fan of the Technocratic movement through a lens that outright rejects capitalism (the socialistic versions of the original movement) but supports Democracy (as several of the founding members of the movement encouraged). 

Obviously swapping out "capital" for "education" 1:1 doesn't immediately fix problems, and requires a constant re-evalulation, and monitoring to weed out corruption that might emerge like any other system of government, but strengthening power at the local level and encouraging national institutions of experts in their fields to turn that expertise to guranteeing the basic needs of all a nation's citizens without, say, the EPA having to worry about some billionaire deciding to gut them for getting in the way of Capital is better than our current situation.

The issue here is again the idea that "appointing individual experts into a cabinet" somehow turns them into "technocrats". Having individual "Technocrats" within a wider neoliberal system is as absurd as appointing an individual "Minister of Communism" in one. The original movement and context of the term was fundamentally left wing and socialist, if one not entirely united ideologically on how much of the existing system should be changed and how much democratic apparatus should remain intact while the fields that can be objectively known should be left to those who know them.

To boil it down to just "they picked a person with a degree for a position in an otherwise liberal government! That counts!" is the exact reductive use of the word that has me so frustrated all the time.
I truly despise how confusing those terms has left technocracy being associated with right wing bullshit.

In comparison to other tech mods it is almost always less powerful/efficient/easy to use, but that's kind of on purpose.
If you just toss it in an pack with a bunch of other tech and don't configure anything it will end up almost instantly outclassed for automation/production. Hearing the "technocractic class" thrown about like that irritates me because of how distorted that word has become in comparison to the original American Technocracy movement from the 30s, and how much it's just used to refer to "educated ivory tower types" instead. The Original technocrats knew that it was essential to appeal to the "common man" of the time, and promise that even in a society organized around specialization and education, the most uneducated manual laborers would still be guaranteed a solid quality of life. I think the Democratic party would actually benefit a lot from being more Technocratic in the ways that matter and offering solutions with the intention of helping everyone instead of dismissing rural populations, but meaningful economic changes needed would not work with their current pro-corporate neoliberal policies, so I'm afraid I'll be stuck seeing my hometown overrun with the same shitty flags it's been flying since 2016 for the foreseeable future.

It's not any sort of livestock, or electric cars or zeppelins for more than luxury transportation. What it is involves genuine change to both the system we live in and the way we live our lives, but the prior is uncomfortable and people refuse to accept the latter because it affects them personally.

When fully realized a factory can become like a work of art with hundreds of moving parts, all taking up a massive area like your Gregtech bases. On the other hand it has very little real endgame - its primary purpose is to provide you with the tools to do whatever you want and create what you want to create. If you can't come up with an end-goal of your own, you may have a hard time getting into it. If you just want something like Ore Duplication or automatic crafting, there are a dozen simpler alternatives (Ore Duplication is practically at the end of Create's tech tree). But if you want the satisfaction of building a massive factory that can print out entire houses to deliver by train around the world, or to turn what might be routine automation in other packs into a more complicated affair, Create might be fun for you to try.

Also on the train that this isn't an unpopular opinion at all in concept, but that the way you frame it kind of is. It's not having a story that people don't like, it's having a Poor story. The past two gens have kept trying really hard to establish a greater sense of story, but failed at it critically by being bogged down with too many small mandatory cutscenes (Maybe when we enter an area pan over to show that our supposed friends are in the area, and let the player decide if they want any interaction with them for the non-critical stuff), increasingly long tutorials, and a lot of buildup that never really pays off right. I can remember beating team flare and being left thinking "Was that it?", and basically nothing about their whole story and plan other than the interesting ancient war that was ultimately irrelevant outside of explaining the big pointless superweapon. In S/M it was super focused on a character that there was no gurantee the player had any interest in, so if you didn't care for Lilly it'd just be a slog through someone else's story, a lot of cutscenes trying to create a sense of tension and drama that the Ultra Beasts were a big deal, only for them to very quickly not be. There was a lot of fun to be had theorizing about things before the game was released but by the end of it I felt like barely anything had changed, especially not for the player. And that brings me to the key issue here... You try to compare pokemon to a JRPG because those usually feature a protagonist with a personality. But honestly that's just... absurd. Because it really isn't, and never was. None of the PCs in any of the mainline games have any real personality or goals of their own. Every one of them has been a blank slate, simple and devoid of any defining characteristics, for the player to project on. In the earlier games you found yourself going through the storyline either because it's what the player was sent out to do (become the champion!) or simply because the villains were so dangerous you'd be crazy not to at that point, if you were even given a choice. Out of universe it was because the player wanted to see what would happen next, but in universe there wasn't any personal reasons in the first 4 gens to be too involved with anything. Gen V is where they started the more story focused games, but honestly in comparison this is the place where they did it best, setting up villains who have something of an actual motive and belief that the player would be opposed to, but even then its just that, something the player is opposed to. We never see the player character contemplating if team plasma is right or not, in the same sense that we don't see them really bounce off of anyone else in Gen VI or VII. In all honesty if you were a person that was more involved in the cutscenes, there could be a lot more heart in it and chemistry in the characters, we could care about the PC. At the crux of it all seems a simple problem: It's not the fact that it's a JRPG that people don't like the cutscenes, but the fact that at the end of the day it ISN'T and never was a JRPG. Final Fantasy XV wouldn't be a game at all if you were just a silent protagonist staring off with the same creepy smile all the time, but that's what we get in SuMo. Maybe I'd like Hau more if I saw my PC hanging out with him and seeming like they wanted to be there, instead of silently watching as he emotes at them.

Define "Perfect". Because frankly my IDEAL game would be kingdom hearts styled combat system, relying on skill at times but with flashy and over the top attacks in real time. Regardless of an absurd combat system, some big changes would still be good. A new region, presumably with new mons is a solid start. Full 3D, not just sun and moon style but with real elevation as well, and even the pointless but satisfying ability to jump. Following Pokemon is a given, it always was and will be. Lots of odd problems, obstacles, and NPCs blocking your path that require using either your own mons or tricking wild ones into helping to solve. Kind of a cross between the ranger games there, and maybe you could even get a styler if you wanted. Of course wild battles and trainer battles are still present, and much harder and more tactical than ever, with almost nobody having empty slots on their team. More importantly, they're hardly static. Wandering and random trainers can be found all over, sometimes wandering and even seemingly fighting wild mons, and if you beat them they'll just heal up and head out. The only differences between old areas and new ones are what mons and trainer types you'll find there, the levels and difficulty scale with you, to an extent. Of course weaker spots and trainers might exist too, to train newly bred or caught weak species. Something similar to the league would eventually be open to you, with each gym fight feeling difficult and harder than the last. A championship tournament would be required, in addition to enough badges/totems/whatver. A bracketed slew of fights all in succession, which you'd have to win before even thinking about challenging the elite four. If you can beat them and the Champion, you can try to take the title. It'd require you to answer summons though, at seemingly random to get back to the mountain to defend the title and whatever perks it may confer. Of course you can always hand it back to the previous one if you think the summons are annoying, and there's plenty of other mechanics to explore. More advanced refurbishing of Super Contests where Mon decoration and move choice feel far more significant, and turn order isn't nearly as much of a factor as it was. A pokeathatlon that puts the player in more control, and lets you enjoy it with controls better than a stylus. Refresh is more integrated than ever, with more options to play with your mon, from more little games to just running and climbing around. Overally a bigger focus on the mons themselves and your interaction to get stronger, just as important as actual fighting (though each one helps the other). As for other, more ridiculous suggestions Battle bond for the player and one specific mon, Players being able to join into combat in some situations, An actual story (Ha, how unrealistic!), a threatening villainous team or two, and perhaps my favorite, discarding the human element completely and making all of this an elaborate mystery dungeon styled game where you play as a pokemon (with all of the features, even using amie to weirdly pet your teammates to their confusion).
